- $\text{curl}\,F$ points in the positive $z$-direction.
after.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{curl}\,F$ denotes the curl of the vector field $F.$

To understand intuitively whether a vector field has curl at a point $P$, imagine that our vector field $F$ represents the velocity field of a stream of flowing water. We place a paddlewheel at $P$ with the axis of rotation pointing in the $z$-direction, and we note whether the paddlewheel rotates or not.

- If the paddlewheel does not rotate due to the action of the water, then the velocity field has zero curl, i.e., $\text{curl}\,F=0.$

- If the paddlewheel is forced to rotate due to the action of the water, then the vector field has curl, i.e., $\text{curl}\,F\ne 0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064672/assets/594106633e422d24b9fea113d24fb6367fdef5ac52724931860e4163e33ce992.png)

If $\text{curl}\,F=0$ everywhere in ${R}^{3}$, we say that $F$ is irrotational.

With that in mind, let's check each statement:

- Statement II is true, whereas statement I is false. If a paddlewheel were placed at any point $P$ in the manner described above, it would rotate. Therefore, $\text{curl}\,F\ne 0.$

- Statements III is true. Since $\text{curl}\,F\ne 0,$ the vector field $F$ is not irrotational.

- Statement IV is false. Using our right hand, if we wrap our fingers in the direction of rotation (clockwise), our thumb will point into the screen. Therefore, $\text{curl}\,F$ also points into from the screen, in the direction of decreasing $z.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given that $F(x,y)=({y}^{2}+{e}^{x})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,j,$ what is the scalar curl of $F?$
after.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+{e}^{x}) \\  & =y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2y \\  & =y(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Scalar Curl of a Vector Field
content.problem: Given that $F(x,y)=({y}^{2}+{e}^{x})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,j,$ what is the scalar curl of $F?$
content.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+{e}^{x}) \\  & =y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2y \\  & =y(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2).\end{aligned}
$$
